note: Campaign #446 W3-B fresh per-arch validation for compute_cap 9.0, run against the CURRENT flash surface (the arch-freshness gate reported all four VALIDATED_SMS entries stale against this campaign's flash-surface edits). That failure is NOT arch-specific — sm_86, sm_89 and sm_90 (this artifact) all panic on the SAME test, the SAME element index, with BYTE-IDENTICAL cpu/cuda/bound values, so it is a defect in this campaign's own new f16 oracle (added at c8612300, campaign-only — not on main), not a property of this device. It is committed as the honest record that the arch WAS exercised at this tip — the device, driver, checkpoint and every other leg are proven — and that exactly one leg is red for a reason the arch does not own. legs.name: jammi-kernels full suite (cuda,flash-attn) — flash + cuda parity incl. this wave's new f16 oracles
legs.note: cuda_parity: 133 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored. Verbatim: thread 'softmax_parity_f16_row_length_regimes' panicked at crates/jammi-kernels/tests/cuda_parity.rs:412:9: softmax f16 dscores[35]: cpu -0.0010614395 vs cuda -0.0010671616 (bound 1.9073486e-6). Reached at row length n=514 (the >512 multi-block regime); the n=510 and n=512 regimes are clean (max|delta|=0) and every FORCED-DEFECT control fires far above bound, so the oracle discriminates — the bound is what the n=514 dscores arm exceeds. Identical on sm_86 and sm_89.

legs.command: JAMMI_KERNELS_STRICT=1 cargo test -p jammi-ai --features cuda,flash-attn,live-gpu-tests --test gpu_capability capability_surface -- --nocapture
